title: Postmortem follow-up: Oct 26 outage
next_steps: Redwood to share final postmortem doc and patch notes by 2026-11-04
Customer and Redwood to run a joint load test w/ production traffic patterns week of 2026-11-08
Schedule reliability workshop to review autoscaling and KV cache behavior (2 hours)
action_items: Priya Nair (Redwood SE): push runtime memory-leak patch to staging and schedule prod deploy by 2026-11-03
Jordan Hayes (AE): send updated SLO and pricing implications for Dedicated vs Hosted on high-QPS routes by 2026-11-02
Maya Ortiz (Nova SRE): provide representative traffic replay (logs + replay script) by 2026-11-05
Ethan Cole (CSM): coordinate reliability workshop and invite infra + security stakeholders by 2026-11-06
summary: Follow-up to the Oct 26 production incident: discussed root cause (KV cache thrash + autoscaler misconfiguration + runtime memory leak), mitigations deployed, monitoring gaps, and next steps including a patch, joint load test, and a reliability workshop. Customer prioritized stability; Redwood committed timelines for fixes and follow-up artifacts.
transcript: 00:00 Jordan Hayes: okay thanks everyone for joining, uh we'll keep this to about 45 minutes. 00:08 Tom Becker: yeah appreciate it, busy day but want to make sure we close the loop on the outage last monday the 26th. 00:16 Priya Nair: quick agenda, recap timeline, root cause, what we deployed already, and propose next steps, and then open for q&a. 00:24 Maya Ortiz: sounds good. 00:30 -- Recap / Timeline -- 00:32 Jordan Hayes: timeline we have in the doc but quick version — 10:12am spike in 95th latency, by 10:20 p99 started failing on read-heavy routes, 10:25 alerts escalated, 10:40 we added temporary routing to an older model variant to mitigate, full restoration at 11:10 after rolling restart and kv cache warmup. 00:55 Maya Ortiz: we saw a compounding effect; as requests retried our KV cache miss-rate shot up and nodes OOMed. 01:04 Priya Nair: and there was an edge case in our continuous batching where a rare sequence length pattern prevented proper kv-ttl cleanup — that's the memory leak we found. 01:18 Tom Becker: so it was three things then? autoscaler settings, cache thrash, and runtime issue? 01:24 Priya Nair: yep, those three interacting. autoscaler had a very tight policy (min nodes too low, scale step too small), during the spike new pods couldn't come up fast enough, existing pods accumulated state. 01:36 Liam Park: to be clear does this affect both hosted and dedicated? 01:40 Priya Nair: primarily affected older Dedicated pools with tighter autoscale configs; hosted accounts saw elevated latency but our global fallback routing helped reduce error rates. 01:52 Rina Shah: from security perspective any data exposure? were any logs containing PII leaked? 01:58 Priya Nair: we audited the logs — no PII surfaced, KV entries are ephemeral and encrypted; we will share the audit snippet in the postmortem document. 02:09 -- Mitigations already applied -- 02:10 Priya Nair: we deployed three things same day: increased autoscaler buffer for the affected Dedicated pool, forced cache compaction/eviction policy changes, and a hotfix that reduces in-memory KV retention for sequences over the threshold. 02:25 Jordan Hayes: that hotfix was a partial mitigation — it prevents immediate OOMs but doesn't fully fix the underlying leak path. 02:33 Maya Ortiz: after the hotfix and restart we saw p99 back to baseline in ~35 mins which is good, but we're nervous about recurrence. 02:41 Priya Nair: agreed, which is why we're prioritizing the runtime patch (fixing the leak) and a more conservative autoscale policy. 02:49 -- Monitoring / Alerts -- 02:51 Maya Ortiz: we didn't have an alert on sustained KV miss-rate increase, only on pod OOMs and response errors. we need earlier indicators. 02:59 Priya Nair: we'll add alerting for sustained miss-rate > 5% over 5m, and a synthetic check for prefix-warmup time. 03:07 Tom Becker: also need cost impact analysis — autoscaling buffers would add spend, we need tradeoffs. 03:13 Jordan Hayes: we'll provide a run-rate delta between current and proposed configs and show Dedicated vs Hosted options for those routes. 03:19 -- Documentation & Compliance -- 03:21 Rina Shah: we need SOC2-relevant artifacts: audit timeline, log excerpts, patch notes, and evidence of deployment. 03:29 Ethan Cole: we'll attach the audit snippet and the deployment runbook to the postmortem. 03:34 Priya Nair: note — some proper nouns in the automated transcript may be off (e.g., kv-cache as "k v cash"), we'll send a cleaned doc. 03:42 -- Customer questions / objections -- 03:44 Tom Becker: our legal team will ask about SLAs and credits; what is Redwood's stance? 03:49 Jordan Hayes: for Dedicated contracts we can discuss credits proportionate to SLA misses per our terms; i'll follow up with legal and include options in the doc. 03:57 Samir Gupta: curious if this is a recurring class of issue; are we tracking regressions post-deploy? 04:02 Priya Nair: yes, we're adding regression monitors tied to our eval harness and will run nightly smoke prompts against canaries. 04:10 Maya Ortiz: i want a clear rollback plan if the runtime patch introduces unexpected behavior. 04:15 Priya Nair: agreed — patch will land to staging, then canary 10% for 24h with synthetic workload and immediate rollback automations. 04:23 -- Shared artifacts referenced -- 04:25 Jordan Hayes: i'll share the postmortem google doc (link: https://redwood.co/postmortems/nova-2026-10-26), the runtime patch PR, and a replay script for the traffic sample (link: https://drive.redwood.co/replays/nova-traffic-10-26). 04:40 -- Recap & Next steps -- 04:42 Jordan Hayes: recap — Priya to push runtime fix to staging and target prod by 2026-11-03, Jordan to send SLO/pricing tradeoffs by 2026-11-02, Maya to provide traffic replay by 2026-11-05, Ethan to schedule reliability workshop by 2026-11-06. 04:58 Tom Becker: thanks, please make the timelines firm in the doc. 05:03 Maya Ortiz: and please include a short executive summary for our CISO. 05:08 Jordan Hayes: will do. 05:12 -- Close -- 05:13 Jordan Hayes: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with the artifacts and confirm the workshop date. 05:18 Tom Becker: thanks all. 05:21 (call ends)\n\nNote: transcript contains minor transcription artifacts; proper nouns and acronyms may be slightly off in the automated export.
